newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 24.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** Indian term lending institutions slash their prime lending rates to 16.5 percent per annum from 17.0 percent with effect from October 23, the Industrial Development Bank of India said on Wednesday
Other term lending institutions included Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India, SCICI and Industrial Finance Corporation
** An indefinite strike over a wage dispute launched by about
one million telephone and postal workers on Wednesday partially disrupted operations in the country's financial markets

Government officials said the stir affected trunk calls, postal services, administrative operations and phone enquiries Operations of some banks were hit by the strike, but stock markets in Bombay were not affected by the stir, dealers said

** Cumulative investment by foreign institutional investors on Indian bourses stand at $6.87 billion as on October 18, while net monthly investments in the same period stood at $85 million, according to sources in the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Economic Times reports

** Indian stock markets staged a smart rally for the second consecutive day on Wednesday, with the 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange surging 114.73 points or 3.56 percent to end at 3,341.86.
** The 100-share National Index was up 48.81 points or 3.41 percent to 1,480.0

** Ford Credit International Inc, the wholly-owned subsidiary of Ford Motor Credit Company of the U.S. has picked up 40 percent equity in a joint venture with Kotak Mahindra Finance at a premium of nearly 3,500 rupees per share, says the Financial Express
** Long-term lender SCICI and state-run Gujarat State Fertiliser Corporation are expected to announce first half results for 1996/97 (April-March) on Thursday
** Fiat Auto will be introducing the sedan version of the Project A 178 in India, the Business Standard reports
Fiat Auto will be investing $600 million on a greenfield
project with an installed capacity of 100,000 cars a year. Pune in India's western Maharashtra state is the front-runner site for the project, the paper says

** The 5.8 billion rupee Dabur India Ltd has entered into a technical collaboration with Shkibo of Japan for its new plant, coming up at Alwar in Rajasthan to manufacture printing guargum, used in the textile industry, the Financial Express reports
